# Democratic pressure (IDD-Mex Dimensión I)

I am turning the IDD-Mex **Índice Democracia de los Ciudadanos** (Dimensión I) state scores into a democratic-pressure layer for the Gulf of California.

The Índice de Desarrollo Democrático de México (IDD-Mex) evaluates democratic development across Mexico's 32 states. Dimensión I covers the effective exercise of citizen rights and situations that violate them (political adhesion / vote, political rights, civil liberties, gender in government, insecurity, and — in later editions — citizen commitment). Indicator and dimension scores are built on a **0–10** scale (10 = best performance among states that year; 0 = worst). I divide by 10 to get **0–1**, then invert so **1 = maximum pressure (weakest citizen democracy)**.

**Pros:** state series back to 2010; Dimensión I is already oriented toward rights / liberties / insecurity; published long sheet makes cleaning easy.  
**Cons:** state level only; indicators are relative within each year (best = 10, worst = 0), so year-to-year levels are not fully cardinal; no 2016 edition in this workbook (we carry 2015 forward); full methods annex lives on idd-mex.org, which has been hard to load.

We assess this at the state level for now (same decision as IEDMX governance, IPS social stability, labor poverty, ENCIG). GoC states: Baja California, Baja California Sur, Sonora, Sinaloa, Jalisco, and Nayarit.

---

**To download / refresh:**

- Series workbook: `SERIES_POR_DIMENSION_y_POR_INDICADOR_IDD_MEX_2010-2024.xlsx`
- Bring it into Mazu at `/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/_raw_data/IDD-MEX/d2026`
- Background: [KAS IDD-Mex](https://www.kas.de/es/web/mexiko/statische-inhalte-detail/-/content/idd-mex); methods notes also appear in the annual IDD-Mex reports (e.g. IDD-Mex 2023 PDF).

---

*Outline of the script:*

1. Read CONAPO population for year-specific weights (needed when Region_9 spans two states).  
2. Read sheet `D I 2010-24` (Índice Democracia de los Ciudadanos by state × year).  
3. Keep GoC states, rescale 0–10 → 0–1, invert to pressure, and fill the missing 2016 year.  
4. Map onto GoC `rgn_id`s and save.  
5. Explore with `plotly`.

---

year_min <- 2010L
year_max <- 2024L

# Dimensión I raw scores are 0-10; OHI wants 0-1
score_max <- 10

goc_states <- c(
  "Baja California",
  "Baja California Sur",
  "Sonora",
  "Sinaloa",

## What Dimensión I covers

From the IDD-Mex materials we have on hand:

| Theme | Role in Dimensión I |
|---|---|
| Adhesión política (voto) | Political adhesion / electoral support |
| Derechos políticos | Political rights |
| Libertades civiles | Civil liberties |
| Género en el gobierno | Gender in government |
| Inseguridad | Conditioning of rights/liberties by insecurity |
| Compromiso ciudadano | Citizen commitment (present in later editions) |

Dimensiones III (Social) and IV (Económica) are **not** used here: those are expressed as deviations from the national mean (can be negative) and feed the composite IDD-Mex differently. Dimensión I stays on the 0–10 indicator scale and enters the composite more directly.

**Orientation for OHI:** raw Dimensión I is higher = better citizen democracy. After `/10`, `pressure = 1 - score` so higher pressure = weaker Dimensión I.

## 1. CONAPO state population (year-specific weights)

Same as in the governance / IPS / ENCIG scripts: sum `POB_TOTAL` so each GoC state-year has one population weight. Needed when Region_9 inherits both Jalisco and Nayarit.

```{r conapo-read}
conapo_raw <- read_csv(conapo_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r conapo-aggregate}
state_population <- conapo_raw %>%
  select(CLAVE_ENT, NOM_ENT, ANO, SEXO, POB_TOTAL) %>%
  filter(NOM_ENT %in% goc_states) %>%
  group_by(year = ANO, estado = NOM_ENT) %>%
  summarize(poblacion = sum(POB_TOTAL, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r conapo-check}
state_population %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2010, 2015, 2020, 2024)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = poblacion) %>%
  kable(
    caption = "CONAPO projected total population (GoC states; selected years)",
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )

stopifnot(all(goc_states %in% unique(state_population$estado)))
```

## 2. Read Dimensión I long series

Sheet `D I 2010-24` has:

- Row 1: title (`Índice Democracia de los Ciudadanos`)
- Row 2: year headers (`2010` … `2024`; **2016 is missing**)
- Rows 3+: one state per row, then one score per year

```{r explore-sheets}
excel_sheets(idd_path) %>%
  tibble(sheet = .) %>%
  kable(caption = "Sheets in the IDD-Mex series workbook")
```

```{r read-dim1-raw}
dim1_raw <- read_excel(idd_path, sheet = dim1_sheet, col_names = FALSE)

dim1_raw %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  kable(caption = "First rows of D I 2010-24 (raw)")
```

```{r clean-dim1}
# Row 2 holds year headers. read_excel may drop a leading empty Excel column,
# so locate the estado column as the one just before the first year header.
header_row <- dim1_raw %>%
  slice(2) %>%
  unlist(use.names = FALSE)

year_cols <- which(!is.na(suppressWarnings(as.integer(header_row))))
years_in_sheet <- as.integer(header_row[year_cols])
estado_col <- min(year_cols) - 1L

stopifnot(estado_col >= 1, length(years_in_sheet) >= 1)

dim1_long <- dim1_raw %>%
  slice(3:n()) %>%
  mutate(
    estado = str_trim(as.character(.[[estado_col]]))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(estado), estado != "") %>%
  select(estado, all_of(year_cols)) %>%
  # rename year columns to calendar years before pivoting
  set_names(c("estado", as.character(years_in_sheet))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -estado,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "score_0_10"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    score_0_10 = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(score_0_10))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(year), !is.na(score_0_10))

dim1_goc <- dim1_long %>%
  filter(estado %in% goc_states) %>%
  arrange(estado, year) %>%
  group_by(estado) %>%
  # fill the missing 2016 edition (and any other gap) from the prior year
  complete(year = year_min:year_max) %>%
  fill(score_0_10, .direction = "down") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    # 0-10 -> 0-1; higher score = better citizen democracy
    score = score_0_10 / score_max,
    score = pmin(pmax(score, 0), 1),
    # OHI pressure: higher = worse
    pressure = 1 - score,
    pressure = pmin(pmax(pressure, 0), 1)
  )

stopifnot(all(goc_states %in% unique(dim1_goc$estado)))
stopifnot(all(year_min:year_max %in% unique(dim1_goc$year)))
```

```{r dim1-checks}
dim1_goc %>%
  count(estado) %>%
  kable(caption = "Rows per GoC state (expect one per year 2010-2024)")

dim1_goc %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(pressure)),
    min_raw = min(score_0_10, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_raw = max(score_0_10, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_pressure = min(pressure, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_pressure = max(pressure, na.rm = TRUE),
    years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "GoC Dimensión I summary (raw 0-10 and pressure 0-1)")

dim1_goc %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  arrange(desc(pressure)) %>%
  select(estado, year, score_0_10, score, pressure) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "2024 GoC Dimensión I (raw, 0-1 score, pressure)")
```

## 3. Map onto `rgn_id` and save

State pressure values are inherited by every GoC `rgn_id` in that state (`municipality_to_rgnid_update.csv`). Region_9 spans Jalisco and Nayarit, so I take a CONAPO population-weighted mean of the two state scores.

```{r mun-rgn-lookup}
mun_lookup <- read_csv(mun_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    estado = str_trim(estado),
    rgn_id = as.character(rgn_id)
  )

estado_to_rgn <- mun_lookup %>%
  distinct(estado, rgn_id) %>%
  mutate(estado_key = str_to_upper(estado)) %>%
  select(estado_key, rgn_id)

estado_to_rgn %>%
  arrange(rgn_id, estado_key) %>%
  kable(caption = "Estado to rgn_id (unique pairs from municipality lookup)")
```

```{r state-to-rgn}
dim1_rgn <- dim1_goc %>%
  mutate(estado_key = str_to_upper(estado)) %>%
  left_join(estado_to_rgn, by = "estado_key", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(state_population, by = c("year", "estado")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rgn_id), !is.na(pressure))

democratic_pressure <- dim1_rgn %>%
  group_by(rgn_id, year) %>%
  summarise(
    # Region_9 is the only multi-state region; weight by CONAPO population
    pressure = if (n() == 1 || all(is.na(poblacion))) {
      mean(pressure)
    } else {
      weighted.mean(pressure, w = poblacion, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    n_states = n_distinct(estado),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rgn_num = as.integer(str_remove(rgn_id, "Region_")),
    pressure = round(pressure, 4)
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, rgn_num) %>%
  select(rgn_id, year, pressure)

democratic_pressure %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Democratic pressure by rgn_id (2024)")
```

```{r save}
write_csv(
  democratic_pressure,
  file.path(output_dir, "democratic_pressure_iddmex_dim1.csv")
)
write_csv(
  democratic_pressure,
  file.path(github_dir, "democratic_pressure_iddmex_dim1.csv")
)
```

## 4. Explore with plotly

### Pressure by state

```{r plot-state}
plot_state <- plot_ly(
  dim1_goc,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~pressure,
  color = ~estado,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers",
  text = ~paste0(
    estado, "<br>", year,
    "<br>raw Dim I: ", round(score_0_10, 3),
    "<br>pressure: ", round(pressure, 3)
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Democratic pressure (1 - IDD-Mex Dimensión I, divided by 10) for the GoC states",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Pressure (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05)),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Estado"))
  )

plot_state
```

### Raw Dimensión I (0–10) by state

```{r plot-raw}
plot_raw <- plot_ly(
  dim1_goc,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~score_0_10,
  color = ~estado,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "IDD-Mex Índice Democracia de los Ciudadanos (raw 0-10), GoC states",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Dimensión I score (0-10)", range = c(0, 10.5)),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Estado"))
  )

plot_raw
```

### Regional pressure time series

```{r plot-rgn}
rgn_labels <- c(
  "Region_1" = "Western Upper Gulf",
  "Region_2" = "Western Midriff Islands",
  "Region_3" = "Western Central Gulf",
  "Region_4" = "Western Southern Gulf",
  "Region_5" = "Eastern Upper Gulf",
  "Region_6" = "Eastern Midriff Islands",
  "Region_7" = "Southern Sonora Coast",
  "Region_8" = "Sinaloa Coast",
  "Region_9" = "Southeastern Gulf"
)

rgn_colors <- c(
  "Region_1" = "#C03729",
  "Region_2" = "#E68C7C",
  "Region_3" = "#FC8F24",
  "Region_4" = "#dcaa38",
  "Region_5" = "#cbd2a0",
  "Region_6" = "#98a25a",
  "Region_7" = "#747428",
  "Region_8" = "#627391",
  "Region_9" = "#8d61a9"
)

plot_rgn <- democratic_pressure %>%
  mutate(
    region = recode(rgn_id, !!!rgn_labels),
    region = factor(region, levels = unname(rgn_labels))
  ) %>%
  plot_ly(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~pressure,
    color = ~region,
    colors = setNames(unname(rgn_colors), unname(rgn_labels)),
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines+markers"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Democratic pressure by GoC region (IDD-Mex Dimensión I inverted)",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Pressure (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05)),
    legend = list(title = list(text = "Region"))
  )

plot_rgn
```
